mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a monotonic recovery trend over the last three weeks (-60.4 to -50.7), indicating sustained momentum in consumer mobility that is expected to persist and push RETAIL_REC further upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from -60.4 to -50.7 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite three consecutive weeks of prior improvement, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in WORKPLACES mobility above a -46 threshold signals restored commuting activity that generates incidental retail visits near office districts, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -46 for the week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -49.3 to -45.3 over the four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses above -46, the threshold trigger is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL time-at-home and rise in TRANSIT usage indicates households substituting home confinement for outside errands, jointly driving increased RETAIL_REC visits over the next four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 19.4 to 16.0 while TRANSIT improved from -60.0 to -55.1
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase when both RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT improves concurrently over consecutive weeks, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime characterized by simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and PARKS, relaxed restrictions on public gathering are inferred to also loosen retail capacity limits, producing an immediate one-week uptick in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved steadily while PARKS rebounded from 27.1 to 40.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following simultaneous WORKPLACES and PARKS gains, the policy-linkage hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound in the most recent week (27.1 to 40.3) reflects a seasonal outdoor-activity surge that temporarily substitutes for indoor retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks until the seasonal effect fades.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped 13.2 points in the latest week after two weeks of decline
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite a PARKS surge exceeding 10 points, the substitution hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilizing GROCERY_PHARM mobility (hovering near -17 for three weeks) suggests essential-trip demand has plateaued, implying any further RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks reflects genuine discretionary spending recovery rather than noise in essential trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM values held between -15.4 and -17.4 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, the discretionary-recovery hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT improves by more than 4 points week-on-week, it signals a behavioral shift toward resuming public transit for shopping trips, producing a same-week or next-week increase in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by 4.3 points from t-3w to t-2w and by 2.0 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week of a TRANSIT jump exceeding 4 points, the threshold hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Joint sustained improvement across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and declining RESIDENTIAL over four weeks indicates a coordinated policy-driven reopening that compounds to drive a stronger four-week rise in RETAIL_REC than any single series would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show consistent directional improvement across the four-week snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no greater than what WORKPLACES alone would predict, despite joint improvement in all three series, the compounding interaction hypothesis is rejected.
